back_translation: Send the tribute lambs to the ruler of the land, from Sela through the wilderness to the mountain of the Daughter of Zion.
Like scattered birds shoved from the nest, so are the daughters of Moab at the fords of the Arnon River.
"Please give counsel; please render a decision. Make your shade like nighttime at high noon. Hide the outcasts; do not betray the refugees.

Let the outcasts of Moab sojourn among you; please be a shelter to them from the destroyer." When the extortioner has come to an end, the destruction has ceased, and the trampler has vanished from the land,
then a throne will be established in steadfast love, and one will sit on it in faithfulness, in the tent of David — a judge who seeks justice and is swift to uphold righteousness.
We have heard of Moab's pride — he is exceedingly arrogant — his conceit, his pride, and his seething insolence; but his boasts are all empty.
Therefore let Moab wail for Moab; let everyone wail together. Moan for the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth, like men utterly crushed.

For the fields of Heshbon have withered, and the vine of Sibmah too. The lords of the nations have trampled its choice branches, which once stretched as far as Jazer and wandered into the wilderness; its shoots spread out wide and crossed over as far as the sea.

Therefore I weep together with the weeping of Jazer for the vine of Sibmah. O Heshbon and Elealeh, I will drench you with my tears, for the joyful shout over your summer fruit and your harvest has fallen silent.
Joy and gladness are taken away from the fruitful orchard; in the vineyards there is no singing, no shouting. No treader treads wine in the presses anymore; I have silenced that joyful vintage-shout.
Therefore my inmost being moans for Moab like the sound of a lyre, and my heart within me for Kir-heres.
And it will be like this: when Moab appears, wearied, on the high place, when he enters his sanctuary to pray, he will gain nothing at all.
This is the word that the LORD spoke concerning Moab in former times.

But now the LORD says: "Within three years, counted like the years of a hired worker, the splendor of Moab will become an object of contempt, with all his great multitude; and the surviving remnant will be tiny and feeble."
